background.label: APOE
background.name: apolipoprotein E
background.definition: APOE is an apolipoprotein, a protein associating with lipid particles, that mainly functions in lipoprotein-mediated lipid transport between organs via the plasma and interstitial fluids (PubMed:14754908, PubMed:1911868, PubMed:6860692). APOE is a core component of plasma lipoproteins and is involved in their production, conversion and clearance (PubMed:14754908, PubMed:1911868, PubMed:1917954, PubMed:23620513, PubMed:2762297, PubMed:6860692, PubMed:9395455). Apolipoproteins are amphipathic molecules that interact both with lipids of the lipoprotein particle core and the aqueous environment of the plasma (PubMed:2762297, PubMed:6860692, PubMed:9395455). As such, APOE associates with chylomicrons, chylomicron remnants, very low density lipoproteins (VLDL) and intermediate density lipoproteins (IDL) but shows a preferential binding to high-density lipoproteins (HDL) (PubMed:1911868, PubMed:6860692). It also binds a wide range of cellular receptors including the LDL receptor/LDLR, the LDL receptor-related proteins LRP1, LRP2 and LRP8 and the very low-density lipoprotein receptor/VLDLR that mediate the cellular uptake of the APOE-containing lipoprotein particles (PubMed:12950167, PubMed:1530612, PubMed:1917954, PubMed:20030366, PubMed:20303980, PubMed:2063194, PubMed:2762297, PubMed:7635945, PubMed:7768901, PubMed:8756331, PubMed:8939961). Finally, APOE also has a heparin-binding activity and binds heparan- sulfate proteoglycans on the surface of cells, a property that supports the capture and the receptor-mediated uptake of APOE-containing lipoproteins by cells (PubMed:23676495, PubMed:7635945, PubMed:9395455, PubMed:9488694). A main function of APOE is to mediate lipoprotein clearance through the uptake of chylomicrons, VLDLs, and HDLs by hepatocytes (PubMed:1911868, PubMed:1917954, PubMed:23676495, PubMed:29516132, PubMed:9395455). APOE is also involved in the biosynthesis by the liver of VLDLs as well as their uptake by peripheral tissues ensuring the delivery of triglycerides and energy storage in muscle, heart and adipose tissues (PubMed:2762297, PubMed:29516132). By participating in the lipoprotein-mediated distribution of lipids among tissues, APOE plays a critical role in plasma and tissues lipid homeostasis (PubMed:1917954, PubMed:2762297, PubMed:29516132). APOE is also involved in two steps of reverse cholesterol transport, the HDLs-mediated transport of cholesterol from peripheral tissues to the liver, and thereby plays an important role in cholesterol homeostasis (PubMed:14754908, PubMed:23620513, PubMed:9395455). First, it is functionally associated with ABCA1 in the biogenesis of HDLs in tissues (PubMed:14754908, PubMed:23620513). Second, it is enriched in circulating HDLs and mediates their uptake by hepatocytes (PubMed:9395455). APOE also plays an important role in lipid transport in the central nervous system, regulating neuron survival and sprouting (PubMed:25173806, PubMed:8939961). APOE is also involved in innate and adaptive immune responses, controlling for instance the survival of myeloid-derived suppressor cells (By similarity). Binds to the immune cell receptor LILRB4 (PubMed:30333625). APOE may also play a role in transcription regulation through a receptor-dependent and cholesterol-independent mechanism, that activates MAP3K12 and a non-canonical MAPK signal transduction pathway that results in enhanced AP-1-mediated transcription of APP (PubMed:28111074). {ECO:0000250|UniProtKB:P08226, ECO:0000269|PubMed:12950167, ECO:0000269|PubMed:14754908, ECO:0000269|PubMed:1530612, ECO:0000269|PubMed:1911868, ECO:0000269|PubMed:1917954, ECO:0000269|PubMed:20030366, ECO:0000269|PubMed:20303980, ECO:0000269|PubMed:2063194, ECO:0000269|PubMed:23620513, ECO:0000269|PubMed:23676495, ECO:0000269|PubMed:2762297, ECO:0000269|PubMed:28111074, ECO:0000269|PubMed:30333625, ECO:0000269|PubMed:6860692, ECO:0000269|PubMed:7635945, ECO:0000269|PubMed:7768901, ECO:0000269|PubMed:8756331, ECO:0000269|PubMed:8939961, ECO:0000269|PubMed:9395455, ECO:0000269|PubMed:9488694, ECO:0000303|PubMed:25173806, ECO:0000303|PubMed:29516132}.

claims.headline: Bionaut Labs is developing a magnetically guided microrobot to deliver drugs to brain tumors
claims.summary: Bionaut Labs is developing a small device that doctors would guide through the spine into a brainstem tumor, release a drug, and retrieve. The company aims to begin clinical trials by 2023, with brainstem gliomas as its initial target. It is also exploring use for Huntington’s disease and other hard-to-reach areas.

claims.headline: Brain-linked system helps a paralyzed man control his hand in a laboratory
claims.summary: A 2016 laboratory demonstration used NeuroLife Neural Bypass Technology: an intracortical implant decoded intended movements and drove an external neuromuscular stimulation sleeve. A participant with quadriplegia from cervical spinal-cord injury made voluntary wrist, hand and finger movements and manipulated objects after training. This was an early human demonstration, not a cure for paralysis or evidence of independent use outside the system.

claims.headline: Trastuzumab deruxtecan was reported as newly available on the NHS for advanced HER2-low breast cancer
claims.summary: The Mirror reported that NICE recommended Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan) for routine NHS use in around 1000 people with HER2-low advanced breast cancer, after a two-year charity campaign. claims.headline: Daraxonrasib improved survival outcomes versus chemotherapy in a phase 3 pancreatic cancer trial
claims.summary: The May 2026 Dana-Farber report describes phase 3 results for daraxonrasib as second-line treatment for previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer. In 500 patients, median overall survival was 13.2 months with daraxonrasib versus 6.7 months with chemotherapy, and median progression-free survival was 7.2 versus 3.6 months. It also reports response and safety results and says a separate trial is evaluating the drug as a possible first-line treatment.

background.label: GSK3B
background.name: glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta
background.definition: Constitutively active protein kinase that acts as a negative regulator in the hormonal control of glucose homeostasis, Wnt signaling and regulation of transcription factors and microtubules, by phosphorylating and inactivating glycogen synthase (GYS1 or GYS2), EIF2B, CTNNB1/beta-catenin, APC, AXIN1, DPYSL2/CRMP2, JUN, NFATC1/NFATC, MAPT/TAU and MACF1 (PubMed:11430833, PubMed:12554650, PubMed:14690523, PubMed:16484495, PubMed:1846781, PubMed:20937854, PubMed:9072970). Requires primed phosphorylation of the majority of its substrates (PubMed:11430833, PubMed:16484495). In skeletal muscle, contributes to insulin regulation of glycogen synthesis by phosphorylating and inhibiting GYS1 activity and hence glycogen synthesis (PubMed:8397507). May also mediate the development of insulin resistance by regulating activation of transcription factors (PubMed:8397507). Regulates protein synthesis by controlling the activity of initiation factor 2B (EIF2BE/EIF2B5) in the same manner as glycogen synthase (PubMed:8397507). In Wnt signaling, GSK3B forms a multimeric complex with APC, AXIN1 and CTNNB1/beta-catenin and phosphorylates the N-terminus of CTNNB1 leading to its degradation mediated by ubiquitin/proteasomes (PubMed:12554650). Phosphorylates JUN at sites proximal to its DNA-binding domain, thereby reducing its affinity for DNA (PubMed:1846781). Phosphorylates NFATC1/NFATC on conserved serine residues promoting NFATC1/NFATC nuclear export, shutting off NFATC1/NFATC gene regulation, and thereby opposing the action of calcineurin (PubMed:9072970). Phosphorylates MAPT/TAU on 'Thr-548', decreasing significantly MAPT/TAU ability to bind and stabilize microtubules (PubMed:14690523). MAPT/TAU is the principal component of neurofibrillary tangles in Alzheimer disease (PubMed:14690523). Plays an important role in ERBB2-dependent stabilization of microtubules at the cell cortex (PubMed:20937854). Phosphorylates MACF1, inhibiting its binding to microtubules which is critical for its role in bulge stem cell migration and skin wound repair (By similarity). Probably regulates NF-kappa-B (NFKB1) at the transcriptional level and is required for the NF-kappa-B-mediated anti- apoptotic response to TNF (TNF/TNFA) (By similarity). Negatively regulates replication in pancreatic beta-cells, resulting in apoptosis, loss of beta-cells and diabetes (By similarity). Through phosphorylation of the anti-apoptotic protein MCL1, may control cell apoptosis in response to growth factors deprivation (By similarity). Phosphorylates MUC1 in breast cancer cells, decreasing the interaction of MUC1 with CTNNB1/beta-catenin (PubMed:9819408). Is necessary for the establishment of neuronal polarity and axon outgrowth (PubMed:20067585). Phosphorylates MARK2, leading to inhibition of its activity (By similarity). Phosphorylates SIK1 at 'Thr-182', leading to sustainment of its activity (PubMed:18348280). Phosphorylates ZC3HAV1 which enhances its antiviral activity (PubMed:22514281). Phosphorylates SNAI1, leading to its ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation (PubMed:15448698, PubMed:15647282, PubMed:25827072, PubMed:29059170). Phosphorylates SFPQ at 'Thr-687' upon T-cell activation (PubMed:20932480). Phosphorylates NR1D1 st 'Ser-55' and 'Ser-59' and stabilizes it by protecting it from proteasomal degradation. Regulates the circadian clock via phosphorylation of the major clock components including BMAL1, CLOCK and PER2 (PubMed:19946213, PubMed:28903391). Phosphorylates FBXL2 at 'Thr-404' and primes it for ubiquitination by the SCF(FBXO3) complex and proteasomal degradation (By similarity). Phosphorylates CLOCK AT 'Ser-427' and targets it for proteasomal degradation (PubMed:19946213). Phosphorylates BMAL1 at 'Ser-17' and 'Ser-21' and primes it for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation (PubMed:28903391). Phosphorylates OGT at 'Ser-3' or 'Ser-4' which positively regulates its activity. Phosphorylates MYCN in neuroblastoma cells which may promote its degradation (PubMed:24391509). Regulates the circadian rhythmicity of hippocampal long-term potentiation and BMAL1 and PER2 expression (By similarity). Acts as a regulator of autophagy by mediating phosphorylation of KAT5/TIP60 under starvation conditions, activating KAT5/TIP60 acetyltransferase activity and promoting acetylation of key autophagy regulators, such as ULK1 and RUBCNL/Pacer (PubMed:30704899). Negatively regulates extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway via death domain receptors. Promotes the formation of an anti-apoptotic complex, made of DDX3X, BRIC2 and GSK3B, at death receptors, including TNFRSF10B. The anti-apoptotic function is most effective with weak apoptotic signals and can be overcome by stronger stimulation (PubMed:18846110). Phosphorylates E2F1, promoting the interaction between E2F1 and USP11, stabilizing E2F1 and promoting its activity (PubMed:17050006, PubMed:28992046). Phosphorylates mTORC2 complex component RICTOR at 'Ser-1235' in response to endoplasmic stress, inhibiting mTORC2 (PubMed:21343617). Phosphorylates mTORC2 complex component RICTOR at 'Thr-1695' which facilitates FBXW7-mediated ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of RICTOR (PubMed:25897075). Acts as a negative regulator of smoothened signaling by mediating phosphorylation of GLI2 and GLI3 in absence of smoothened, promoting their processing by the SCF(BTRC) complex (PubMed:16705181). Phosphorylates FXR1, promoting FXR1 ubiquitination by the SCF(FBXO4) complex and FXR1 degradation by the proteasome (By similarity). Phosphorylates interleukin-22 receptor subunit IL22RA1, preventing its proteasomal degradation (By similarity). Phosphorylates and inhibits the CTP synthase and protein-asparagine deamidase activities of CTPS1 (PubMed:17681942). claims.headline: ER-100 phase 1 update reports tolerability and preliminary visual-field changes in glaucoma participants
claims.summary: January 2026 coverage described planned human testing of ER-100 for glaucoma after animal studies. In October, Life Biosciences reported a Day 56 safety update in three adults with open-angle glaucoma given intravitreal ER-100. Oral doxycycline induced its gene expression for eight weeks; it was an activation agent, not a separate experimental glaucoma treatment. Two participants had preliminary visual-field improvements. This early, uncontrolled safety cohort does not establish efficacy.

claims.headline: EU approves erenumab to prevent migraine in patients with at least four attacks a month
claims.summary: European regulators approved erenumab for migraine prevention. The article says it blocks a receptor thought to be involved in migraine activation, is injected monthly with a home-use pen, and halved average monthly migraine days in trials. The manufacturer said private access in the UK was expected from September 2018.

claims.headline: How a cross-continent effort brought an Ebola vaccine from lab research to use in outbreaks
claims.summary: The article traces the development of the VSV-based Ebola vaccine from early research in Germany, Canada and the United States through testing during the West African epidemic. It describes animal protection, a Guinea ring-vaccination trial, later use in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and regulatory approvals in Europe and the United States.

claims.headline: Study reports rapid symptom improvement with nasal esketamine for depression
claims.summary: A trial of 68 people at imminent risk of suicide found greater improvement in depressive symptoms among those given nasal esketamine alongside hospital care and antidepressants than among those given placebo. The difference was seen during the first four weeks, but effects had levelled out by day 25. Phase three trials were underway before possible licensing.

reported_statements.text: Nasal esketamine alongside hospital care and antidepressants was associated with greater improvement in depressive symptoms than placebo during the first four weeks.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: Symptom improvements were reported within the first 24 hours, while the treatment effect had levelled out by day 25.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: It could provide a rapid option for severely depressed people at imminent risk of suicide, particularly early in treatment.
reported_statements.speaker: researcher

reported_statements.text: Rare side effects may require assessment in larger studies.
reported_statements.speaker: other_expert

reported_statements.text: An outside FDA advisory panel recommended that the FDA approve esketamine.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: The nasal-spray antidepressant is described as fast-acting.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: It is being tested for major depressive disorder and suicidal thinking.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: If approved, it could be the first major advance in depression treatment since Prozac was introduced in 1987.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: The nasal spray is intended for people with severe depression, especially those with suicidal thoughts.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: Two major clinical trials did not find the treatment more effective than placebo.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: It acts on the brain in ways similar to ketamine but does not affect some key neurological receptors.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: If approved, it could become the first new major-depression treatment introduced for clinical use in more than 30 years.
reported_statements.speaker: article

claims.summary: The FDA approved esketamine, developed by Johnson & Johnson, as a new treatment option for people with depression that has not responded to existing therapies. It was tested alongside oral antidepressants, and experts said it might work faster than current antidepressants.

claims.headline: An mRNA therapy that reawakens heart muscle cells was reported to improve heart function in mice after a heart attack
claims.summary: The Mirror reported a University of Cambridge study in mice, published in Nature Cardiovascular Research, in which short-lived mRNA injected into the heart temporarily activated two proteins (Myc and Cyclin T1) so heart muscle cells divided and helped repair damage. Treated mice had a stronger heartbeat and about 10 per cent more blood pumped per beat than mice given a mock treatment. The researchers say it is not a complete cure and describe it as an early step towards a possible heart failure treatment.

background.label: RNA, Messenger
background.definition: RNA sequences that serve as templates for protein synthesis. Bacterial mRNAs are generally primary transcripts in that they do not require post-transcriptional processing. Eukaryotic mRNA is synthesized in the nucleus and must be exported to the cytoplasm for translation. Most eukaryotic mRNAs have a sequence of polyadenylic acid at the 3' end, referred to as the poly(A) tail. The function of this tail is not known for certain, but it may play a role in the export of mature mRNA from the nucleus as well as in helping stabilize some mRNA molecules by retarding their degradation in the cytoplasm.

claims.headline: The injection bepirovirsen was reported to be approved by the FDA as the first treatment offering a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B
claims.summary: The FDA approved GSK's bepirovirsen, an injection given for about six months, for chronic hepatitis B. In two Phase 3 trials, 19% of treated adults still had no detectable viral protein 24 weeks after stopping all treatment, against under 1% on standard care. The article stresses that this is a functional cure, not clearance of the virus.

claims.headline: Keratin films repaired early enamel lesions in laboratory tests
claims.summary: A 2025 laboratory study used wool-derived keratin films to guide mineral growth on artificially demineralized, extracted human teeth. The repaired enamel showed changes in structure and mechanical properties. This was not a trial of treatment in patients or whole-tooth regrowth. Toothpaste and professionally applied gels were proposed future uses; clinical benefit and durability were not established by this study.

claims.headline: Researchers link ketamine’s rapid, lasting antidepressant effects to changes in cell signaling
claims.summary: A University of Illinois at Chicago team reports that ketamine quickly shifts G proteins out of cell-membrane lipid rafts in a cellular model. The researchers propose that this may explain its fast and lasting effects; the article also describes symptom improvement in clinical-study participants who had not responded to standard antidepressants.

reported_statements.text: Maintaining ketamine's benefit has been difficult and has so far required repeated doses.

reported_statements.text: Long-term use could bring safety or misuse problems that a registry may help identify.

reported_statements.text: Further research is needed to establish how best to use ketamine for depression.

reported_statements.text: A course of infusions followed by oral doses was associated with sustained improvement in around 40% of cases.

reported_statements.text: When it works, ketamine can ease depression within hours rather than weeks.

reported_statements.text: About half of patients given intravenous ketamine respond, and roughly half of those responders achieve full remission.

reported_statements.text: A small preliminary study found that cognitive behavioral therapy alongside ketamine may extend mood improvement compared with ketamine alone.
reported_statements.speaker: researcher

reported_statements.text: Participants experienced dissociative effects from ketamine, including when they had received naltrexone.

reported_statements.text: Earlier studies found that ketamine can improve depression symptoms within hours.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: Repeated or widespread ketamine use for depression could carry risks of abuse or dependence.

reported_statements.text: Ketamine can be used to treat severe depression.

background.label: Malaria
background.definition: A protozoan disease caused in humans by four species of the PLASMODIUM genus: PLASMODIUM FALCIPARUM; PLASMODIUM VIVAX; PLASMODIUM OVALE; and PLASMODIUM MALARIAE; and transmitted by the bite of an infected female mosquito of the genus ANOPHELES. Malaria is endemic in parts of Asia, Africa, Central and South America, Oceania, and certain Caribbean islands. It is characterized by extreme exhaustion associated with paroxysms of high FEVER; SWEATING; shaking CHILLS; and ANEMIA. Malaria in ANIMALS is caused by other species of plasmodia.

background.label: Peptides
background.definition: Members of the class of compounds composed of AMINO ACIDS joined together by peptide bonds between adjacent amino acids into linear, branched or cyclical structures. OLIGOPEPTIDES are composed of approximately 2-12 amino acids. Polypeptides are composed of approximately 13 or more amino acids. PROTEINS are considered to be larger versions of peptides that can form into complex structures such as ENZYMES and RECEPTORS.

reported_statements.text: Successful Phase 3 trials could lead to MDMA becoming a prescription treatment for PTSD.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: The article describes MDMA as safe and therapeutically effective when given to people with PTSD.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: Participants on higher doses had greater average decreases in PTSD symptom severity than those on lower doses.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: One year after the study, 16 of 26 participants were no longer classified as having PTSD, while two had received a PTSD diagnosis again.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: Reported side effects included anxiety, headache, fatigue, muscle tension, insomnia and temporary increases in suicidal thoughts.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: MDMA may enhance psychotherapy and could have a future role in PTSD treatment.
reported_statements.speaker: researcher

reported_statements.text: Short-term MDMA use with close medical and psychological supervision seems safe for carefully selected people with PTSD.
reported_statements.speaker: other_expert

reported_statements.text: Average PTSD assessment scores fell from 92 at enrollment to 31 at the 12-month follow-up.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: Average assessment scores fell a further 9.6 points between treatment completion and the 12-month follow-up.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: The trial enrolled people whose PTSD had persisted for an average of nearly 30 years despite prior conventional treatments.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: Adult mice given MDMA later spent more time in places associated with other mice and their bedding than untreated mice did.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: The social behavior observed after one dose was still evident two weeks later in the mice.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: Some studies suggest that after one MDMA-assisted therapy session, up to 76% of trauma survivors no longer meet PTSD diagnostic criteria.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: Ten U.S. clinics were expected to start providing the therapy through expanded access.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: Fifty patients had initially been approved to receive expanded-access treatment.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: Data from expanded-access patients may be considered in decisions on final market approval, including reports of adverse events.
reported_statements.speaker: article

background.label: Melanoma
background.definition: A malignant neoplasm derived from cells that are capable of forming melanin, which may occur in the skin of any part of the body, in the eye, or, rarely, in the mucous membranes of the genitalia, anus, oral cavity, or other sites. It occurs mostly in adults and may originate de novo or from a pigmented nevus or malignant lentigo. Melanomas frequently metastasize widely, and the regional lymph nodes, liver, lungs, and brain are likely to be involved. The incidence of malignant skin melanomas is rising rapidly in all parts of the world. (Stedman, 25th ed; from Rook et al., Textbook of Dermatology, 4th ed, p2445)

reported_statements.text: In people with melanoma removed by surgery, adding the vaccine to Keytruda lowered the risk of recurrence or death by 42% compared with Keytruda alone.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: The vaccine uses mRNA customized to tumor markers to prompt an immune response against cancer cells.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: A participant suspected the vaccine caused mild flu-like symptoms and feeling down the next day, but she did not know whether she received vaccine or placebo.
reported_statements.speaker: patient

reported_statements.text: It may strengthen the immune response by mobilizing additional killer T cells to recognize the tumor.
reported_statements.speaker: other_expert

reported_statements.text: It may help some patients, though an expert said the available data do not yet establish it as a major new treatment.
reported_statements.speaker: other_expert

reported_statements.text: The vaccine plus Keytruda lowered melanoma-spread risk by 38% over two years compared with Keytruda alone.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: After two years, 82.2% of patients given the vaccine with Keytruda were cancer-free, compared with 70% given Keytruda alone.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: The vaccine uses material from each patient’s tumour to train the immune system to identify cancer cells for attack.
reported_statements.speaker: article

reported_statements.text: The approach could improve outcomes for advanced melanoma and other cancers where current immunotherapies work poorly.

background.label: Multiple Sclerosis
background.definition: An autoimmune disorder mainly affecting young adults and characterized by destruction of myelin in the central nervous system. Pathologic findings include multiple sharply demarcated areas of demyelination throughout the white matter of the central nervous system. Clinical manifestations include visual loss, extra-ocular movement disorders, paresthesias, loss of sensation, weakness, dysarthria, spasticity, ataxia, and bladder dysfunction. The usual pattern is one of recurrent attacks followed by partial recovery (see MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS, RELAPSING-REMITTING), but acute fulminating and chronic progressive forms (see MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS, CHRONIC PROGRESSIVE) also occur. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p903)

claims.headline: Survodutide was reported to reduce belly and liver fat in a Phase 3 obesity trial
claims.summary: The Mirror reported results from the Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-1 trial of survodutide, a once-weekly injection acting on glucagon and GLP-1 receptors. People with obesity but without type 2 diabetes lost up to 16.6 per cent of body weight over 76 weeks at the top dose, and a separate analysis found visceral fat down by up to 34 per cent and liver fat by up to 63.1 per cent. The article quotes a pharmacist saying the drug is still investigational and not approved, and notes the body-composition analysis involved a relatively small group.

background.label: Obesity
background.definition: A status with BODY WEIGHT that is grossly above the recommended standards, usually due to accumulation of excess FATS in the body. The standards may vary with age, sex, genetic or cultural background. In the BODY MASS INDEX, a BMI greater than 30.0 kg/m2 is considered obese, and a BMI greater than 40.0 kg/m2 is considered morbidly obese (MORBID OBESITY).

claims.headline: TOFA was reported to cut body fat in obese mice and boost the effect of semaglutide and tirzepatide
claims.summary: The Daily Mail reported that University of California Berkeley researchers found the 1970s compound TOFA makes cells burn fat for energy, in a study in mice published in Science Advances. Obese mice lost about 8.7 per cent of body weight in 24 days on TOFA alone, and much more when it was combined with low doses of semaglutide or tirzepatide, with almost all the loss being fat. The article stresses TOFA has not yet been tested in humans, so its safety profile is unknown.

claims.headline: Eli Lilly reports trial results for daily orforglipron in people with Type 2 diabetes
claims.summary: Eli Lilly said a clinical trial found its daily pill orforglipron had blood-sugar and weight-loss results, and safety data, similar to injectable drugs such as Ozempic and Mounjaro. claims.headline: Removal of the fallopian tubes was reported as a way to lower the risk of ovarian cancer by up to 80 per cent
claims.summary: The Daily Mail reported that experts say removing the fallopian tubes could cut ovarian cancer risk by as much as 80 per cent, because most deadly ovarian cancers appear to start there. The procedure is already offered to high-risk women in a UK national research trial, and health bodies are encouraging doctors to offer it to women over 45 who are having other abdominal surgery. The article notes that 98 per cent of women will not develop ovarian cancer and calls the approach extreme.

articles.title: 'Silent' ovarian cancer kills 4,000 British women every year, but a pioneering new treatment can slash the risk by 80%

background.label: Parkinson Disease
background.definition: A progressive, degenerative neurologic disease characterized by a TREMOR that is maximal at rest, retropulsion (i.e. a tendency to fall backwards), rigidity, stooped posture, slowness of voluntary movements, and a masklike facial expression. Pathologic features include loss of melanin containing neurons in the substantia nigra and other pigmented nuclei of the brainstem. LEWY BODIES are present in the substantia nigra and locus coeruleus but may also be found in a related condition (LEWY BODY DISEASE, DIFFUSE) characterized by dementia in combination with varying degrees of parkinsonism. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1059, pp1067-75)

claims.headline: FDA grants breakthrough designation to single-dose psilocybin research for major depression
claims.summary: The FDA granted the Usona Institute’s Phase 2 trial of a single psilocybin dose for major depressive disorder Breakthrough Therapy designation. The seven-site US trial planned to enroll 80 participants and compare psilocybin with niacin, alongside psychotherapy sessions. The article reports that Usona expected the trial to finish by early 2021, with Phase 3 trials possible if results were positive.

promises.description: Usona estimated its Phase 2 trial would be completed by early 2021.

background.label: Stiff-Person Syndrome

Minor sensory stimuli, such as noise and light touch, precipitate severe spasms. Spasms do not occur during sleep and only rarely involve cranial muscles. background.label: Diabetes Mellitus, Type 2
background.definition: A subclass of DIABETES MELLITUS that is not INSULIN-responsive or dependent (NIDDM). It is characterized initially by INSULIN RESISTANCE and HYPERINSULINEMIA; and eventually by GLUCOSE INTOLERANCE; HYPERGLYCEMIA; and overt diabetes. Type II diabetes mellitus is no longer considered a disease exclusively found in adults. Patients seldom develop KETOSIS but often exhibit OBESITY.

background.label: Caloric Restriction
background.definition: Reduction in caloric intake without reduction in adequate nutrition. In experimental animals, caloric restriction has been shown to extend lifespan and enhance other physiological variables.
